transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-01
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CTO, Moonrise), Zoe Kim (Cloud Eng), Maria Alvarez (Head of Security), Ethan Park (Solutions Architect)

Summary:
Quick technical onramp to prepare Moonrise's listing in Redwood's marketplace and to validate on-prem/VPC deployment patterns. Covered packaging, Helm/OCI artifact expectations, KMS/HSM integration notes, perf benchmarking plan, and tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics covered:
- Marketplace packaging & Helm chart requirements
- Network and KMS integration for Private deployments
- Quantization & runtime tradeoffs for latency/cost
- Benchmarks: what Moonrise will provide for lab runs
- Pilot plan + UAT checklist and runbook handoff

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call, I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Maya Chen our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:09] Raj (Moonrise): Good, thanks. Raj here. We've got Zoe, Maria, and Ethan on too.
[00:14] Jordan: awesome. We're aiming to walk through the marketplace onramp flow, packaging expectations, and a short checklist for the pilot. If anything feels too detailed we can mark for follow-up.
[00:27] Maya (Redwood SE): I'll focus on the deployment and runtime side — how the Marketplace expects images, Helm charts, and some of the network/KMS constraints when customers pick "Private" or "Dedicated" modes.
[00:38] Raj: Great. High level — Moonrise provides an LLM gateway for enterprise search and has an onprem option with an operator. We're testing listing on Redwood marketplace to make it easier for customers to deploy. Primary asks: simple listing, VPC-friendly install, KMS integration, and a performance profile so customers know latency/cost.
[00:59] Zoe (Cloud Eng): we also have a compliance box — we need to ensure the listing does not require outbound traffic to third-party telemetry endpoints by default.
[01:10] Maria: yes, and we need to validate KMS/HSM compatibility — we use HashiCorp Vault in some customers and AWS KMS in others.
[01:21] Maya: totally, we'll document the KMS adapter patterns, we support both vault and cloud KMSs. For the marketplace package we prefer a helm chart that supports three modes: hosted-sample, dedicated-reference, and private-vpc. The chart should include values for networkPolicy, egress toggles, and KMS provider configs.
[01:42] Ethan: do you have a sample helm chart? We've got a pretty opinionated operator right now.
[01:47] Jordan: Yes, we'll share a sample helm chart and a packaging checklist. I'll drop links in the notes after the call. "link: https://redwood.example/partners/packaging-onramp" (note: internal sample).
[01:58] Raj: great. A couple of concerns from my team: quantization — some customers need int8 for cost but we also ship int16 models. How does Redwood present model variants in the listing?
[02:12] Maya: good question. The listing can show recommended variants and you can add model profiles with a short description. On the runtime, we run quantized and FP16 variants and route by policy. For benchmarking we suggest you provide two artifacts: a full-precision model and a quantized variant with an expected latency/cost table.
[02:32] Zoe: about benchmarking — what's the recommended payload shape? We have both short chat-like requests and longer doc-assist flows.
[02:39] Maya: please provide three representative payloads: short less-than-50 tokens chat, medium 200-token single response, and a long 1k-token summarize. Also include a distribution of concurrency expectations. That helps us pick kernel paths and estimate batch sizing.
[02:57] Raj: we'll export those. Ethan will handle.
[03:02] Ethan: yep I'll get the traces. Any preferred format?
[03:05] Maya: a simple JSON array of requests with timestamps is fine, plus a 5-minute perf trace from your staging cluster — e.g., output from our test harness or raw latency histograms.
[03:15] Maria: on security — SOC 2 is table stakes for our customers. Does Redwood require any extra agent-level telemetry?
[03:22] Jordan: we don't require telemetry to external endpoints by default. For Marketplace listing we have an optional telemetry opt-in. For enterprise private deployments you can disable outbound telemetry and we provide an offline bundle for Marketplace approval. We'll also share our SOC 2 summary and the security integration matrix.
[03:38] Raj: can you call out where we should declare the KMS options in the chart?
[03:42] Maya: under values.yaml: kms.provider, kms.config (URI or secretRef), kms.hsm.enabled true/false. For Vault we recommend a sidecar sync or a CSI provider. Note that CSI name may be mis-typed by some folks as "CSI vault" in docs, we see that in older transcripts — sorry, typo noise.
[04:03] Zoe: talking of sidecars, our infra team wants to avoid extra containers. Can the chart support a CSI-only path?
[04:09] Maya: yes, there's a CSI-only path and a sidecar path. We'll include both examples — sidecar is easier for local dev, CSI is preferred for minimal surface area.
[04:18] Jordan: switching gears to network — for Private deployments we'll need a sample network diagram showing required inbound/outbound rules. Maya, can you show a quick slide?
[04:27] Maya: (screen share described) The flow: clients -> LB -> inference replicas. For private mode, everything in VPC, no public egress, optional NAT for updates. We require the control-plane to be reachable during install for licensing but we can do a bootstrap via signed token to avoid persistent outbound connections.
[04:48] Raj: persistent outbound is a blocker for some of our telco customers. The signed-token bootstrap approach sounds promising — can you expand?
[04:55] Maya: sure — during install you call Redwood's control-plane once to validate license and fetch a signed config blob. After that, the cluster can run fully air-gapped. It's how we handle onprem customers who cannot have long-lived outbound. There may be subtle differences if you use our operator vs static yaml.
[05:14] Ethan: is that available today?
[05:18] Maya: yes, it's in our private deploy flow, we'll put the doc link in the pack.
[05:23] Jordan: quick note — some words in our docs sometimes read "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Dedicated" — ignore that, it's auto transcript artifact, but packaging docs are accurate.
[05:35] Raj: hah, good to know.
[05:38] (small cross talk)
[05:42] Zoe: what's the expected time to onboard a listing in your marketplace? Days, weeks?
[05:47] Jordan: typical self-serve listing we can publish in 2-3 weeks if the helm chart and artifacts are ready; for Private / onprem with KMS integrations and SOC2 checks it's more like 4-8 weeks depending on compliance review. Pilot can be 2 weeks to validate perf.
[06:03] Maria: will there be an additional security review from Redwood for the package?
[06:07] Jordan: yes, lightweight automated checks (image scanning, policy lint) plus a manual ops review for private listings. We'll share the checklist.
[06:16] Raj: ok on to runtime tradeoffs — can we talk about batching vs latency? Some customers insist on low-1xx ms p95 for short prompts.
[06:25] Maya: yes, short prompts need small batch sizes and prefer a latency-first policy. We can configure route policies per SKU: latency-first uses single-token streaming mode and tiny batches; cost-first uses larger batch windows and prefix caching. There's a quant tradeoff too: int8 can save cost but adds a penalty on some ops for certain seq lengths.
[06:48] Zoe: any known issues with Aurora or AMD nodes? We use a mix of instance types.
[06:54] Maya: our runtime has optimized kernels for both NVIDIA and AMD, but quantization paths differ. We'll add a note in the model profile about expected perf per hardware type — i.e., A100 vs L40 vs AMD MI300. If you can share a sample node type we can run targeted lab tests.
[07:11] Ethan: we'll list the node types.
[07:14] (brief pause)
[07:18] Raj: can we commit to a pilot that includes a 2-hour lab with Redwood's SEs? We want to validate a private deploy with Vault and a 50-concurrency scenario.
[07:27] Jordan: absolutely — Maya, can you lead?
[07:30] Maya: yes, I'll run the lab. We'll need the payloads, the helm chart, and credentials for a staging cluster. We won't touch production keys, of course.
[07:40] Maria: we'll need an NDA amendment for keys?
[07:44] Jordan: our standard partner NAT is fine, but if you need an addendum we can loop in legal. For the lab we'll use ephemeral test keys or a staging Vault with tokens.
[07:56] Raj: sounds good.
[08:00] Jordan: quick question — do you plan to offer both managed and onprem versions to customers via the listing?
[08:07] Raj: yes, idea is a single listing with two deployment modes: hosted managed and operator for onprem.
[08:13] Maya: that's a common pattern. We'll recommend separate SKUs in the listing metadata and clear docs on assumptions for each SKU.
[08:22] Zoe: about billing — if a customer picks dedicated capacity, how does billing surface? Flat monthly or usage?
[08:28] Jordan: Dedicated typically uses reserved capacity pricing with a monthly commitment, and the listing metadata can point to Redwood's pricing page. For Marketplace we support both metered usage and committed pricing — you'll need to pick the SKU model. We'll include guidance.
[08:42] Raj: any gotchas on the packaging side we should watch for?
[08:45] Maya: common gotchas: missing CRDs in the chart, non-parameterized secrets, and images not hosted in an OCI-compatible registry. Also ensure bootstrap script handles air-gap installs.
[08:57] Ethan: we use a custom CRD today; is that ok?
[09:01] Maya: custom CRDs are fine but document them and provide default values. Marketplace review will test the upgrade path.
[09:09] Raj: can you share examples of acceptable artifact locations?
[09:12] Jordan: we accept public OCI registries, S3 presigned artifacts, and private registries (with credentials in values). For private listing we prefer vendors to publish manifests in an OSS-friendly registry to ease scanning.
[09:25] (10 minute mark)
[09:28] Maya: quick aside — we sometimes see "KV cash" in auto transcripts; correct term is "KV cache" when we talk about prefix caching; just flagging because I think you'll see some typos in the docs if you import a raw transcript.
[09:40] Raj: lol noted.
[09:43] Jordan: ok moving to runbook and UAT checklist — we'll provide a runbook template with install steps, smoke tests, and diagnostics. The UAT will cover upgrade, scale-up, failover, and KMS rotation.
[09:57] Maria: KMS rotation — we need to ensure you support key rotation without downtime.
[10:02] Maya: yes, both Vault and KMS providers support rolling rotation via CSI or the operator. We'll include a rotation pattern.
[10:10] Raj: what about logging — we want to ensure no PII is sent by default.
[10:15] Jordan: default logs are structured and scrub PII. We'll include config toggles to further reduce telemetry.
[10:22] Zoe: can you show an example performance matrix for a model?
[10:26] Maya: (describes) columns: model_name, variant, hw_type, p50, p95, tokens/sec, memory_gb, cost_estimate_per_million_tokens. We can provide a template.
[10:38] Ethan: how strict is the cost estimate? Customers use it to budget.
[10:42] Jordan: it's an estimate based on batch profiles; we recommend including ranges. Some customers prefer to publish both "expected" and "peak" numbers.
[10:51] Raj: any regulatory notes around EU data residency we should surface?
[10:55] Maya: marketplace metadata allows you to list regions and residency notes. For EU-only customers, we recommend private deploy in an EU region and call that out.
[11:04] Raj: perfect.
[11:06] (midpoint recap)
[11:10] Jordan: recap — Redwood to share packaging checklist and sample helm; Moonrise to provide payloads and perf traces; schedule a 2-hour lab; Redwood to share SOC2/KMS matrix.
[11:23] Raj: agreed.
[11:25] Maya: I'll lead the lab and prepare a quickstart repo.
[11:29] Ethan: I'll gather traces and the operator chart.
[11:33] Maria: I'll confirm KMS provider list and internal compliance notes.
[11:37] Jordan: great. Anything else?
[11:40] Zoe: one last thing — upstream dependency on our operator's CRD versions. We may need to freeze a minor for the marketplace.
[11:47] Maya: marketplace can accept a listing tied to a specific CRD version; upgrades are part of the UAT. We'll document.
[11:55] Raj: ok let's lock the lab date, maybe week of Nov 15th.
[12:00] Jordan: sounds good, I'll ping calendar invites after this.
[12:04] (closing)
[12:07] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the checklist and files.
[51:20] (meeting ends)
